definitions.explanation: Indicates a direction, area, or method.
Used to compare two things, indicating preference or degree.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}は{北|きた}の{方|ほう}にあります。
examples.english: The station is in the north direction.

examples.japanese: お{茶|ちゃ}の{方|ほう}が{好|す}きです。
examples.english: I prefer tea. (Tea is the one I like more.)

examples.japanese: こちらの{方|ほう}が{安|やす}いです。
{海|うみ}の{方|ほう}へ{歩|ある}いた。
{音|おと}は{窓|まど}の{方|ほう}から{聞|き}こえてきた。
examples.english: The sound came from the direction of the window.

examples.japanese: {歩|ある}くより{電車|でんしゃ}の{方|ほう}が{早|はや}いですよ。
examples.english: The train is faster than walking.

notes:
方 (ほう) is used for: 1) Direction or area (北の方 - toward the north), 2) Comparisons (Aの方がBより～ - A is more ~ than B). The comparison pattern is very common: 「Aの方が好き」 (I prefer A), 「こちらの方がいい」 (this one is better).

Note: 方 can also be read かた meaning 'person' (polite) or 'way of doing.'
